guides.title: Studio workflow & capabilities
guides.description: Start here: choose the right script, workspace and data workflow.
guides.markdown:
# Kinetix Studio

Kinetix Studio is a general-purpose market research and backtesting app. The Studio version and KX language version are separate: an application update does not necessarily introduce a new language version.

## A complete workflow

1. Open a project folder from Home or File → Open Folder.
2. Inspect a CSV, JSON or Parquet file in Explorer, or open Data Library → Download to acquire data.
3. Choose Prepare data, add transforms, update the preview and validate the result.
4. Save and register a versioned output in Data Library. Copy its pinned reference for reproducible research.
5. Create an Indicator, Study or Strategy bound to that dataset, then Run.
6. Inspect Problems, Output, chart results, Research Studio and Strategy Tester as appropriate. Save scripts and generated pipeline recipes in your workspace.

## Five script types

| Type | Use it for | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Indicator | Reusable calculations, chart signals and overlays | Series and visual output |
| Study | Investigating data without inventing trades | Charts, tables and research reports |
| Strategy | Testing trading rules with the broker/account model | Trades, orders, positions and performance |
| Pipeline | Reading, downloading, transforming and saving data | Versioned registered datasets |
| Library | Sharing reusable KX functions and utilities | Code imported by other scripts |

The native mutable data operations belong in Pipelines. Study/Strategy execution remains deterministic and does not perform acquisition or native file mutation.

## Three places to keep things

- Workspace: project files, local scripts and data under the folder you opened.
- Kinetix Library: reusable scripts shared across projects in Kinetix Home.
- Data Library: registered datasets, their metadata and reproducible version references. This is different from a Library script.

A workspace-relative path includes every folder from the workspace root to the dataset. It is not relative to the pipeline script's own folder. Copy KX Reference from a preview to avoid guessing.

## Capabilities and where to learn them

| Area | Documentation |
| --- | --- |
| Language syntax, Series, collections, missing values, reusable modules | Language Basics, Language & runtime reference, API Reference |
| Files, imports, global code and project sessions | [Workspaces](WORKSPACES.md) |
| Native file/folder reads, joins, filters, derived columns, validation, versioned saves | [Data engine and pipelines](DATA_ENGINE.md) |
| Provider keys, downloads, pagination, cancellation and resume | [Connections & downloads](V2.3_CONNECTIONS.md) |
| Visual preparation and generated KX | [Visual data preparation](visual-data.json) |
| Editor, chart, panels, settings and desktop builds | [Editor, charts & settings](desktop.json) |
| Broker-aware orders, portfolio capital, intrabar execution and corporate actions | Strategies, Multi-Asset Portfolios, Point-in-Time Data, Language & runtime reference |
| Reports, comparisons, saved runs, sweeps and chronological windows | [Research Studio](RESEARCH_STUDIO.md) |
| Every registered public function, declaration and global | API Reference and searchable namespaces |
| Working code, including nested versioned examples | Examples |

## Limits are part of the documentation

Do not assume every market/provider offers every interval or dataset. A date-only event timestamp does not establish when information became tradable. Portfolio intrabar routing, financing/cross-currency models and full out-of-core execution have documented boundaries. Consult the detailed language/runtime and research references before interpreting a backtest as realistic execution.

guides.title: Editor, charts, settings & builds
guides.description: Use the desktop interface and produce an executable or installer.
guides.markdown:
# Using the desktop app

## Explorer and scripts

Open a workspace folder and use Explorer context menus to create files/folders, rename, move or delete entries. Select the script type when creating a .kx file. Promote reusable scripts to Kinetix Library or copy shared code into the workspace. Delete and Unregister are different: unregistering a native dataset keeps its saved data file.

Middle-click closes editor tabs. Drag .kx files into Studio to import them. Problems/Output stay in the bottom area; eligible panels can be docked into editor tabs. Use the command palette to find available commands.

## Run, Stop and output

Run executes the active script. Read Problems for compiler/runtime diagnostics and Output for logs, native I/O results and saved dataset references. Stop uses the supported runtime cancellation path; download jobs also expose Cancel/Resume in Data Jobs. A long native transform in visual preparation is not a cancellable acquisition job.

Pipeline execution prepares data. Indicators and Studies provide visuals/research output. Strategies produce broker/account results in Strategy Tester. A source file preview is not registration; saving/registering makes the dataset discoverable for other scripts.

## Charts and strategy inspection

Use the chart to inspect plots, named/lower panes, drawings and the OHLCV readout. Script properties provide Inputs, Style and Visibility where supported. Strategies expose trades, orders, open positions, rejection diagnostics, equity/drawdown and portfolio exposure views. Research reports and saved runs add metrics, tables, histograms, comparisons and sweeps.

The broker/runtime reference explains next-eligible-bar fills, order types, sizing, account models, intrabar modes, time/session behavior and portfolio restrictions. Chart display is not proof that a strategy has been causally validated.

## Settings

- General: global Kinetix Home, separate from your open workspace.
- Chart Preview: colors, candle bodies/wicks, grid, axes and free/magnet crosshair.
- Downloads: relative folder, destination, initial date range, preferred connection and optional snapshot reuse.
- Connections: provider profiles, request pacing/retries and masked API-key entry. On Windows, keys remain in Credential Manager rather than workspace scripts.

Reset appearance resets chart appearance while retaining the configured data location/download preferences. Provider/account access is still required for restricted feeds.

## Build or run locally

From the Studio repository, with Node/npm, Rust, Visual Studio C++ build tools and WebView2 installed:

```powershell
npm install
npm run desktop:dev
```

For a production frontend, executable and Windows installer:

```powershell
npm run desktop:build
```

Collected release files are under release/windows. A documentation sync/build does not build or release the desktop app. The package may retain a development-preview suffix until acceptance is complete.

## Troubleshooting

Check the root displayed next to a relative data path. Use the exact path/error and likely correction rather than moving data until it happens to work. For a provider rejection, Edit download and check the symbol, market, timeframe and dates; check saved key/access for authorization errors.

During the v2.4 verification, development-server module requests timed out in one environment; the built frontend completed native desktop workflow testing. A successful production build does not prove that every local development server is healthy. If startup remains on the recovery screen, record the message and terminal output for diagnosis.

guides.title: Workspaces & shared libraries
guides.description: Project roots, Explorer, imports and global reusable code.
guides.markdown:
# Kinetix Studio — Workspaces & Global Library

Desktop Studio supports project folders independently of the global reusable-script library. Native data preparation, downloads and visual workflows complement the same workspace model.

## Two independent roots

Kinetix Studio now distinguishes two filesystem scopes:

1. **Kinetix Home** — the configurable global reusable-resource folder, normally `Documents/Kinetix Studio/`.
2. **Workspace** — an arbitrary project directory opened with **File → Open Folder**.

Opening `F:\Trading\Research\Example Research\` never changes Kinetix Home. Closing that folder leaves the global library available.

### Global Kinetix Home

```text
Documents/Kinetix Studio/
  Indicators/
  Studies/
  Strategies/
  Pipelines/
  Libraries/
  Templates/
```

The five KX script categories are visible under **KINETIX LIBRARY** in Explorer. Connection profiles are managed in Settings → Connections and the Downloads dialog; their configuration/checkpoints live in application data, and keys use Windows Credential Manager.

### Project workspace

A workspace is the actual directory tree on disk. Explorer shows folders, KX scripts, data files, JSON/configuration and other project resources without copying them into Kinetix Home.

```text
Example Research/
  data/
    raw/
    processed/
  scripts/
  strategies/
  studies/
  results/
  kinetix.project.json
```

## Commands

The File menu and command palette provide:

- **File: Open Folder**
- **File: Open Recent**
- **File: New File**
- **File: Save Workspace**
- **File: Close Folder**

Workspace Explorer context actions provide create file/folder, rename, move, delete, copy relative path and **Promote to Kinetix Library**.

Global library KX resources can be copied back into the active project with **Copy to Workspace**.

## Session persistence

Workspace UI state is keyed by the canonical project path. Kinetix remembers:

- open KX tabs;
- active KX file;
- expanded workspace directories;
- the existing global panel/layout state through the normal workspace store.

Recent workspaces are stored in Kinetix application data rather than in project folders.

## `kinetix.project.json`

**File → Save Workspace** writes/updates a small project configuration in the opened project root. v2.1 records the project name, conventional project paths, script-resolution policy and the configured global Kinetix Home.

Example:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "name": "Example Research Research",
  "paths": {
    "data": "./data",
    "scripts": "./scripts",
    "results": "./results"
  },
  "datasets": {},
  "scriptResolution": {
    "workspace": ".",
    "global": "@global/"
  },
  "globalLibrary": {
    "home": "C:\\Users\\Josh\\Documents\\Kinetix Studio"
  }
}
```

Large datasets are not copied into the project merely because a workspace is opened. Dataset registration/version pinning belongs to the Data Library/Data Engine milestones.

## KX path resolution

KX imports now understand physical script location.

### Project-relative

From `strategies/pead_v1.kx`:

```kx
import library util from "../scripts/research/util.kx";
```

resolves relative to the importing file.

### Explicit global library

```kx
import library util from "@global/Libraries/research-util.kx";
```

always resolves from Kinetix Home.

### Explicit workspace root

```kx
import library util from "@workspace/scripts/research/util.kx";
```

always resolves from the active project root.

Legacy basename imports remain supported only when the match is unambiguous. If both a project and global resource could satisfy the same basename, compilation intentionally fails and the author must use a relative, `@workspace/` or `@global/` path.

## Promote to Kinetix Library

Promoting a project KX script:

- copies the physical file into the matching global category;
- keeps the original workspace copy;
- refuses to silently overwrite an existing global resource;
- warns when the promoted script contains relative project dependencies;
- keeps the KX declaration type/category consistent.

The project can then explicitly import the reusable copy with `@global/...`. This avoids silently changing a research project when a global resource later evolves.

## Filesystem safety

Native project operations are restricted to the selected workspace root. Absolute paths, `..` traversal and paths that resolve through symlinks/junctions outside the root are rejected.

Global-library operations are restricted to the configured Kinetix Home and fixed library categories.

## Data workflows in the workspace

Workspace data previews provide Copy KX Reference, pipeline insertion/creation and Prepare data. Pipelines read scoped CSV/JSON/Parquet files or folders through the native data engine; visual preparation builds the same plans. Saved outputs are content-hashed and registered in Data Library. Native registered datasets and completed downloads also open in Prepare data.

Data Library → Download manages connections, provider requests and resumable jobs. The duplicate download activity-rail shortcut was removed in v2.4; Data Library and Home still provide download entry points. See DATA_ENGINE.md and V2.3_CONNECTIONS.md for scoped reads, transforms, immutable versions and acquisition details.

Strategies and historical backtests remain deterministic and do not perform acquisition or mutable native file operations. The generated KX pipeline is the reusable recipe for a visual workflow; save that script before closing the draft.

guides.title: Connections & downloads
guides.description: Provider setup, secure keys, download jobs, cancellation and resume.
guides.markdown:
# v2.3 Data Connections and native acquisition

Development preview: **2.3.0-dev.1**, branch `v2.3-data-connections`. The v2.2 review checkpoint remains on `main` at `e578328`.

## Use the workflow

Open **Download data** on Home, **Data Library → Download**, or the cloud icon. Choose a **Data source**, then enter its inputs once. LSE needs a symbol and From/To dates; Alpha Vantage needs a symbol; the public ZipLime and Quant500 snapshots need no symbol or dates. Choose the destination and **Start download**. The app builds provider paths, parameters, polling and filenames automatically.

If the source needs a connection, **Set up connection** opens the matching provider template. Save your API key in the masked field, then return to the download. Existing saved connections and keys are retained. Public ZipLime and Quant500 connections need no key. Keys and provider pacing can also be managed in **Settings → Connections**. **Settings → Downloads** saves default destination, relative folder, initial date range, preferred connection and snapshot reuse.

**Advanced options** holds output overrides, snapshot reuse and a read-only generated request. Custom HTTP exposes the method, path and parameters it needs; polling, pagination, JSON pointers and checksums stay under Advanced. Provider symbol/date fields and editable query parameters are never shown as duplicate inputs.

**Data Jobs** shows progress and the next useful action. A failed HTTP 400/404 request offers **Edit download**, rebuilding known provider requests from their inputs instead of repeating obsolete defaults. Retry is available for transient failures. Old history receives corrected HTTP guidance too; HTTP 400 is not described as a redirect error. Job paths and technical details are collapsed.

Once complete, **Create pipeline** creates a workspace pipeline that previews, validates, saves a versioned Parquet output and registers it in Data Library. Edit `processed` to add transforms and configure the appropriate dataset kind/time/availability columns before using it for research. Code **Libraries** contain reusable KX functions; **Data Library** contains registered datasets. Pipelines prepare these datasets for Studies and Strategies.

Raw inputs remain separate from processed outputs. Filenames include content hashes. Existing raw and processed files are never overwritten by these operations. The original job location is displayed; a reference from another workspace cannot silently be inserted into the current one.

## Generic HTTP

`data.download(request)` is available only in `pipeline()` scripts. Both compiler and runtime reject native network/data operations from Strategies, including computed access or aliases. Saved datasets remain usable by deterministic backtests, charts and research.

```kx
const downloaded = data.download({
    connection: "provider",
    path: "/prices.csv",
    query: { symbol: "AAPL" },
    outputPath: "data/raw/provider/prices.csv",
    scope: "workspace",
    resumeExisting: true
});
const raw = data.read(downloaded.path, { scope: "workspace", format: "csv" });
```

A connection has an HTTPS base URL, authentication (`none`, `bearer`, header API key or query API key), request interval and maximum GET retries. Query parameters are strings. POST accepts a JSON body. POST is not automatically retried, because repeating a POST can create another provider job. An explicit retry/resume can repeat it.

The raw response streams to disk. The default byte limit is 2 GiB across a job; `maxBytes` can explicitly select up to 100 GiB. Structured JSON record validation is limited to 50 MiB per page. HTTP 429 and transient 5xx responses use bounded retry/backoff, including numeric Retry-After values. Public connections follow up to five HTTPS redirects; authenticated connections do not redirect credentials to another endpoint. Use the final provider origin for authenticated downloads.

`resumeExisting` defaults to false, so a normal request fetches a new snapshot. Opting in reuses a matching completed snapshot only after verifying its raw hashes, or resumes its matching unfinished job. Request identity includes the connection configuration, query/body and output context. Reusing a completed snapshot deliberately does not check for newer provider data. Disable the flag to refresh it.

Cancelled/interrupted GET transfers resume using a strong ETag, If-Range and a verified complete remaining Content-Range. If the server sends a fresh 200 response, Kinetix restarts the partial file. A server without a strong validator is redownloaded rather than spliced onto unknown bytes. A declared SHA-256 must match before publication. Cancellation stops requests, polling, waits and streaming; verification/publication also checks cancellation before committing an output.

## Pagination and chunking

Pagination supports page numbers, offsets and JSON cursors. Supply its query `parameter`, `recordsPointer`, `maxPages`, and a `nextPointer` for cursor mode. Page/offset modes accept `step` and optional `pageSize`; without pageSize they stop on an empty array. Cursor mode stops on an absent/null/empty next cursor. Repeated cursors fail instead of looping indefinitely. Reaching maxPages while more data may remain reports an incomplete job.

Each page is an immutable file in a job-specific raw folder. The checkpoint advances after publication, so restart does not repeat a page that already committed. A completed paginated reference reads only that job's folder. The byte limit covers all pages together.

For date/symbol acquisition, use ordinary KX loops around download requests with `resumeExisting: true`; completed chunks are verified and reused on rerun. `examples/v23/lse-ohlcv-chunks.kx` shows this. `dateWindows()` in the source planner produces inclusive non-overlapping calendar chunks, including leap dates.

## Provider sources

| Source | Implemented request and source reference |
| --- | --- |
| London Strategic Edge | The existing downloader's `/v3/export` contract, X-API-Key, 202 job_id, `/v3/jobs/{id}` polling, ready file download and checksum verification. The provider job ID and resolved file path survive restart. |
| Alpha Vantage | [EARNINGS API](https://www.alphavantage.co/documentation/), query-key authentication from the OS vault, quarterlyEarnings validation. HTTP-200 API error/rate-limit objects are rejected as data. |
| ZipLime | [Publisher dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ZipLime/earnings-calendar), pinned revision `f8d9be6f6b22a107edbd497bb01cf779cc292880`, announcements/earnings Parquet files and publisher SHA-256 values. Update the revision and hashes together to adopt a newer snapshot. |
| Quant500 | [Open data and field dictionary](https://quant500.com/data), `/api/descarga/anuncios.csv`, public CSV with `comment: "#"` for its metadata lines. |

`data.read(..., { recordsPath: ["quarterlyEarnings"] })` reads the nested array through the same native engine. No separate Python transformation engine is introduced. Quant500's time/source/quality flags remain in the data. Alpha Vantage's date-only reportedDate is not assigned a verified intraday availability time. The example retains that limitation in saved metadata.

## Credentials and persistence

Provider keys use Windows Credential Manager under the application identifier, connection ID and provider origin. Changing the provider origin cannot forward the old key. The frontend receives only a configured/not-configured status. Keys entered in the credential field are not stored in profiles.json, workspace snapshots, KX examples or request checkpoints. Request query/body values are saved as job configuration; credentials belong in the connection credential field. Request URLs with embedded credentials and API-key query arguments in scripts are rejected; the native client injects the configured credential at request time. Errors omit provider response bodies and credential-bearing URLs.

Profiles and job checkpoints are under the user's application-data connections directory. Raw files are under the explicitly selected workspace or Kinetix Home. Profiles are global to this app account, not copied into workspace projects. Jobs stop when the application process closes and can resume after reopening; they are not an operating-system background service. OS credential storage currently targets Windows. OAuth/browser login, automatic daily account-budget discovery and provider billing checks are not implemented.

## Examples

- `examples/v23/generic-http.kx`
- `examples/v23/paginated-json.kx`
- `examples/v23/alpha-vantage-earnings.kx`
- `examples/v23/lse-ohlcv-chunks.kx`

LSE and Alpha Vantage contracts are covered by local fixtures. Live authenticated account acceptance must use keys entered by the user in the app; the existing Python script's keys are not imported automatically.

LSE downloads now expose Market and Timeframe dropdowns (US stocks and 1d by default). Options use the official LSE Data 3.0 client market codes and candle resolutions, including 1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 4h and 1d. Edit download restores these choices; older requests retain the original defaults. Market/timeframe appear in generated raw filenames. Forex/crypto slash-pair symbols are preserved in requests and converted to safe filenames. Feed availability still depends on the provider/account. Reference: https://github.com/londonstrategicedge/lse-data/blob/main/lse/data3.py

guides.title: Visual data preparation
guides.description: Preview, transform, validate, register and generate equivalent KX pipelines.
guides.markdown:
# Visual data preparation

## Open a source

Choose Data Library → Prepare data, Prepare data in a workspace file preview, or Prepare data on a completed download. Registered native dataset cards and previews also offer this action. The file must be inside the current workspace or Kinetix Home. Open the matching workspace if a registered file belongs elsewhere.

Source options expose file format, CSV delimiter/header/comment prefix, nested JSON records path and recursive folder reads. Completed-download handoff preserves the saved raw path and provider-specific source options; it does not start another download.

## Preview and transform

Preview returns 25 rows per page without requiring a complete count. Use Previous/Next to inspect pages. Operations still apply to the full dataset; sorting and joins can scan all rows.

| Step | Inputs and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Select columns | Choose the columns to retain |
| Rename column | Choose an existing column and its new name |
| Filter rows | Column, condition and explicitly typed comparison value; use Is missing for nulls |
| Sort rows | Columns in selection order, ascending or descending |
| Remove duplicates | Key columns, first/last policy and optional ordering column |
| Fill missing values | Column and replacement value |
| Calculate column | Output name and a restricted expression such as close * volume |
| Normalize time | Input column/unit, optional output column; converts to epoch milliseconds |
| Normalize daily trading sessions | XNYS session dates, DST-aware open/close, availability and snapshot completion; original timestamps retained |
| Join data | Second scoped file/folder, matching left/right key columns, join type and prefix |
| Resample OHLCV | Millisecond time column, fixed bar interval, price/volume columns and optional symbol grouping |

Add the step, then Update preview. You can edit, reorder and remove steps. Source/step changes mark the previous preview as stale; stale results cannot be paged, validated or saved as the current result.

For a multi-symbol resample, normalize time first and group by symbol. Joins require equal numbers of left/right keys in corresponding order. More complex right-side preprocessing can be added in generated KX.

## Validate and save

Choose a dataset name, relative output path, destination and Parquet or CSV format. Under Dataset time and roles, configure time/availability, timezone, price adjustment, optional symbol/timeframe and OHLCV roles. OHLCV output needs a time column.

Validate full dataset checks the entire result. Review warnings about missing values, duplicate/non-monotonic timestamps and malformed prices. Missing market sessions are not automatically evidence of corruption.

Save and register writes a content-hashed immutable output and registers it in Data Library. Parquet uses ZSTD. Source files and existing saved versions are preserved. The confirmation supplies a pinned data.dataset reference. Inspect the registered preview before using it in research.

## Keep the recipe as KX

Generate KX script reproduces the source options, ordered transforms, preview, validation and versioned save through the existing KX APIs. Choose Copy KX script or Open as pipeline, then save the .kx file. Running it should reproduce the visual result.

Visual drafts live while the dialog is open; they are not automatically saved as reusable recipes. Existing arbitrary KX scripts cannot be reverse-engineered into visual steps. Native operations may scan large data, and this dialog does not provide query cancellation.

## Prepare daily US equity bars

Choose **Normalize daily trading sessions**, select the source timestamp column, then choose its meaning: **UTC date is the vendor's session label** for date-labelled daily files, or **Actual instant → New York local date** for genuine UTC event timestamps. Do not infer the convention solely from the hour displayed in a vendor file.

Enter the **source snapshot cutoff (UTC)** as an ISO timestamp ending in `Z`, for example `2026-10-27T20:30:00Z`. Use the actual time the source was captured, not a later preparation time. A partial daily bar must remain incomplete when reopened tomorrow. Daily availability options expose numeric units, a conservative publication delay and an optional final-publication timestamp column. Calendar close cannot by itself establish vendor finality.

The bundled XNYS regular-session calendar supports 1990–2035, including US daylight saving, holidays, exceptional closures and early closes. Future exceptional closures require a calendar update. Original columns remain unchanged; new session/availability/completion columns appear in the preview. Wide previews scroll horizontally inside the table, while the form stays in place.

After adding the step, update the preview and validate. Calendar-aware missing-session checks exclude weekends and holidays and count internal gaps per `symbol`. Rename a different ticker column to `symbol` first, or prepare one instrument at a time. The operation does not certify missing leading/trailing history outside the observed bounds.

Saving selects session-close time, `available_at`, a daily timeframe and New York timezone automatically. The metadata role `"session_close":"time"` is intentional and unique: it identifies the session timestamp. The separate availability column controls strategy observation. The original vendor timestamp stays available for audit without a competing time role.

Incomplete and non-session rows remain visible in the native preview but cannot enter primary strategy bars or external KX strategy timelines. Normalized daily rows are not intrabar execution data; use genuine intraday bars, trades or ticks for that purpose. Preserve the reserved session safety columns in subsequent transforms. Market activation requires a single instrument.

Generate KX script emits the equivalent `data.normalizeDailyOhlcv()` operation and versioned save. See **KX pipelines & native data engine → Exchange-aware daily OHLCV normalization** for the complete field contract and **pipelines/daily-session-normalization.kx** in Examples for an editable recipe. Replace its example snapshot cutoff before running it.

guides.title: Research Studio
guides.description: Reports, reproducible runs, comparisons, sweeps and chronological windows.
guides.markdown:
# KX Studio v1.9 Research Studio

v1.9 turns the existing deterministic backtester and Study runtime into a repeatable research workflow. The feature set is deliberately strategy-agnostic: the same run/preset/sweep/report tooling can be used for technical systems, multi-asset portfolios, event studies, futures/FX/crypto research, cross-sectional work, or any other KX Study/Strategy.

## Research panel

The bottom **Research** tab contains five views:

- **Current** — current Strategy statistics, passive benchmark summaries, and custom `report.*` output.
- **Runs** — save the current result with its exact KX source and input overrides. Saved runs persist in IndexedDB rather than localStorage so equity/trade/order histories are not constrained by small browser storage quotas.
- **Compare** — compare up to three saved runs. Strategy runs show normalized equity and core metrics; Study/Strategy custom `report.metric()` values are also compared.
- **Sweep** — run one- or two-axis numeric parameter sweeps over `input.int` / `input.float` values. Strategies capture Strategy statistics; Studies and Strategies can both capture `report.metric()` outputs. A sweep is capped at 100 combinations per invocation to protect the UI/runtime.
- **Train / OOS** — run explicit Train, Validation and Out-of-Sample windows, or generate rolling chronological train/test windows. Window runs retain normal indicator warm-up history while broker activity is constrained to the requested Strategy execution window.

The rolling-window runner is an evaluation workflow. It does **not** silently choose the best parameter set on each training period; automated train-optimise-test policy selection is intentionally not inferred by the platform.

## `report.*`

Studies and Strategies can create a Research Report without forcing research into a trade ledger:

```kx
report.metric("Average return", averageReturn, { format: "percent" });
report.table("Buckets", ["Bucket", "N", "Return"], rows);
report.line("Forward return", forwardReturnSeries);
report.histogram("Distribution", returnSeries);
```

Supported calls:

- `report.metric(label, value, options?)`
- `report.table(title, columns, rows)`
- `report.line(title, series, options?)`
- `report.histogram(title, series, options?)`

`report.*` is captured once for the research result; it is not multiplied by the Strategy's sequential per-bar broker evaluation.

## Inputs, presets, Style and Visibility

The script settings panel now has:

- **Inputs** — current `input.*` values, grouped with optional `group` and `tooltip` metadata.
- **Style** — UI overrides for plot colour/line width.
- **Visibility** — show/hide individual script plots without editing KX source.

Input presets save the current overrides by script and can be reapplied later. Plot UI overrides are separate from KX source and do not mutate the script.

Example:

```kx
const fast = input.int("Fast EMA", 20, {
  min: 5,
  max: 80,
  step: 5,
  group: "Signal",
  tooltip: "Fast trend length"
});
```

## Passive benchmarks

Strategies may declare one or more passive benchmark datasets:

```kx
strategy({
  name: "Portfolio Research",
  dataset: "PORTFOLIO_CLOCK",
  benchmarks: [
    "BENCHMARK_A",
    { dataset: "BENCHMARK_B", label: "Reference B" }
  ]
});
```

Kinetix reports benchmark return, Strategy return and excess return over the Strategy equity range. Benchmarks are reference series; they do not consume portfolio capital or create broker positions.

## Cross-sectional helpers

v1.9 adds generic research helpers:

```kx
stats.zscore(value, values)
stats.rank(value, values, "desc")
stats.percentileRank(value, values)
```

These operate on numeric arrays/Series and are not tied to any market, strategy or event type.

## Independent plot scales

`priceScale` is honored by Chart Preview:

```kx
plot.line(primarySeries, { title: "Price model", priceScale: "right" });
plot.line(auxiliarySeries, { title: "Unrelated scale", priceScale: "none" });
```

- `right` uses the normal right scale.
- `left` uses a visible left scale.
- `none` gives that plot an independent overlay scale without a visible axis.

Named/lower panes continue to work with `pane:`.

## Strategy Tester additions

v1.9 adds:

- portfolio gross-exposure %, net-exposure %, and concurrent-position charts;
- passive benchmark comparison summaries;
- richer selected Trade and Order inspectors;
- visible rejection diagnostics and machine-readable rejection codes;
- Trades, Equity and Orders CSV exports.

The diagnostics can explain broker/order rejections such as insufficient capital, maximum positions, invalid price/tick, or minimum quantity. Kinetix does not claim to infer why an arbitrary user-written boolean expression evaluated false; that requires explicit script/report instrumentation.

## Persistence and reproducibility

A saved research run stores:

- script/file identity;
- exact source text;
- input overrides;
- optional execution window;
- Strategy report including equity/trades/orders when applicable;
- custom Research Report output.

Saved research runs and sweeps use IndexedDB. Small UI configuration such as input presets and plot overrides remains lightweight local UI state.

## Validation

Run:

```bash
npm run engine:check
npm run integrity:test
npm run research:test
```

`research:test` covers `report.*`, grouped input metadata, Strategy execution windows, passive benchmarks, cross-sectional stats helpers and research persistence fallback behaviour.

guides.title: Language & runtime reference
guides.description: Detailed language, broker, portfolio and causal-data behavior.
guides.markdown:
# KX Language Foundation — KX 2.1

KX is the controlled TypeScript-like scripting language used by standalone **KX Studio**. Scripts do not receive unrestricted DOM, network, filesystem, browser or Tauri access. Market/research data enters through the Data Library and KX data APIs.

## v2.1 workspace-aware imports

KX scripts now retain physical scope/path metadata when used in the desktop IDE. Import paths resolve deterministically:

```kx
// relative to the importing project file
import library localUtil from "../scripts/local-util.kx";

// explicit active-workspace root
import library projectUtil from "@workspace/scripts/project-util.kx";

// explicit reusable global Kinetix Home
import library sharedUtil from "@global/Libraries/shared-util.kx";
```

Legacy basename-style imports remain compatible only when exactly one script matches. If a workspace resource and a global library resource share the same basename, KX reports the import as unresolved/ambiguous instead of silently choosing one. This makes project reproducibility explicit when reusable libraries are present.


## Script types

### Indicator

Indicators are reusable calculation/signal modules.

Generic Indicator:

```kx
indicator({
  name: "VWAP",
  overlay: true
});

const value = ta.vwap(close, volume);
plot.line(value, { title: "VWAP" });
export value;
```

Bare `open/high/low/close/volume/time` are generic Series inputs in this form. The file can compile/validate without loading market data and resolves those inputs from a parent Study/Strategy when imported.

Optional standalone visual binding:

```kx
indicator({
  name: "VWAP",
  dataset: "eur_usd_1d",
  overlay: true
});
```

A dataset-bound Indicator executes against that imported OHLCV dataset and opens Chart Preview for visual validation.

### Pipeline

Pipelines are KX data-engine programs. They may read approved workspace/global files, build lazy DuckDB-backed transformations, preview/validate results and save immutable registered dataset versions.

```kx
pipeline({ name: "Prepare Earnings" });
const raw = data.read("data/raw/earnings.parquet", { scope: "workspace" });
const clean = data.dedupe(raw, ["symbol", "fiscal_period"], { keep: "last" });
data.save(clean, {
  name: "earnings_pti",
  path: "data/processed/earnings.parquet",
  format: "parquet",
  versioned: true,
  kind: "fundamentals"
});
```

Native filesystem/data-mutation APIs are intentionally restricted to `pipeline()` scripts. A Study or Strategy using `data.read()`, `data.save()` or another native pipeline operation fails compilation with `KX5008`; historical backtests must consume already-created datasets rather than making mutable file/network calls.

### Study

Studies are visual/research programs. They can import Indicators, declare primary OHLCV, load any number of secondary datasets, create plots/panes/drawings and emit structured research output. They do not execute orders.

```kx
study({
  name: "Earnings Research",
  dataset: "eur_usd_1d",
  overlay: true
});

const earnings = data.dataset("earnings_results");
const surprise = earnings.eps_actual - earnings.eps_estimate;
plot.line(ta.ema(close, 20), { title: "EMA 20" });
```

### Strategy

Strategies are visual scripts with deterministic broker/backtest execution.

```kx
strategy({
  name: "EMA Cross",
  dataset: "eur_usd_1d",
  initialCapital: 100000,
  currency: "USD",
  commissionType: "percent",
  commission: 0.0001,
  slippage: 0,
  pyramiding: 1,
  defaultQtyType: "percent_equity",
  defaultQtyValue: 100
});

const fast = ta.ema(close, 20);
const slow = ta.ema(close, 50);

if (ta.crossover(fast, slow)) {
  strategy.entry("Long", strategy.long);
}
if (ta.crossunder(fast, slow)) {
  strategy.close("Long");
}
```

A Strategy **must** declare a primary OHLCV `dataset:`. Dataset economics (`pointValue`, `tickSize`, `currency`) are inherited automatically and may be overridden in the Strategy declaration.

## Strategy API — v1.8.6

### Directions

```kx
strategy.long
strategy.short
```

### Entries

Market entry:

```kx
strategy.entry("Long", strategy.long);
strategy.entry("Short", strategy.short);
```

Optional per-entry sizing overrides:

```kx
strategy.entry("Long", strategy.long, { qty: 2 });
strategy.entry("Long", strategy.long, { qtyPercent: 25 });
```

Pending limit entry:

```kx
strategy.entry("Pullback", strategy.long, { limit: limitPrice });
```

Pending stop entry:

```kx
strategy.entry("Breakout", strategy.long, { stop: triggerPrice });
```

Stop-limit entry:

```kx
strategy.entry("Breakout Pullback", strategy.long, { stop: triggerPrice, limit: limitPrice });
```

Generic directional order (net/reduce/reverse current exposure as required):

```kx
strategy.order("Adjust", strategy.short, { qty: 2 });
```

A pending order remains live until it fills, is replaced by another order with the same ID, or is cancelled. A stop-limit entry supplies both `stop` and `limit`; if the stop triggers intrabar but the OHLC path cannot prove a later limit fill, KX conservatively waits for a subsequent bar.

### Cancellation

```kx
strategy.cancel("Pullback");
strategy.cancelAll();
```

### Market close / scale-out

```kx
strategy.close("Long");
strategy.close("Long", { qty: 1 });
strategy.close("Long", { qtyPercent: 50 });
strategy.closeAll();
```

The first argument to `strategy.close()` references an entry ID. Quantity and percentage overrides support partial market exits.

### Protective stop / target

```kx
strategy.exit("Long Risk", "Long", {
  stop: stopPrice,
  limit: targetPrice
});
```

Equivalent `from` object form is also accepted:

```kx
strategy.exit("Long Risk", {
  from: "Long",
  stop: stopPrice,
  limit: targetPrice
});
```

`stop` and `limit` accept numeric scalars or `Series<number>`. Multiple `strategy.exit()` IDs may coexist for scale-outs. Exit quantity can be controlled with `qty` / `qtyPercent`, and a trailing exit can use `trailPoints` plus optional `trailOffset`.

```kx
strategy.exit("Target 1", "Long", { qtyPercent: 50, limit: target1 });
strategy.exit("Runner", "Long", { trailPoints: 4, trailOffset: 2 });
```

### Live broker state

Broker state is evaluated sequentially on each completed bar:

```kx
strategy.positionSize
strategy.positionAvgPrice
strategy.cash
strategy.availableCash
strategy.buyingPower
strategy.equity
strategy.openPnl
strategy.positionSide
strategy.pendingOrders
strategy.openPositions
strategy.grossExposure
strategy.netExposure
strategy.grossExposurePct
strategy.netExposurePct
```

For a single-instrument Strategy, `strategy.positionSize` is signed (positive long, negative short, zero flat). In a v1.8.6 portfolio Strategy, the unqualified `positionSize`/average/side refer to the primary Strategy instrument while the shared account fields refer to the complete portfolio. Named instruments are inspected with:

```kx
strategy.position("asset_b_1d")
strategy.positionSizeOf("asset_b_1d")
strategy.positionAvgPriceOf("asset_b_1d")
strategy.openPnlOf("asset_b_1d")
strategy.positionSideOf("asset_b_1d")
```

`strategy.cash` / `strategy.availableCash` are shared account cash in portfolio mode; entering a cash instrument reserves full notional while a margin instrument reserves configured margin capital.

### Strategy declaration options

Useful Strategy options include:

```kx
strategy({
  name: "Example",
  dataset: "es_1m",
  instruments: [
    "nq_1m",
    { dataset: "gc_1m", capitalModel: "margin", marginRate: 0.10, pointValue: 100, quantityStep: 1 }
  ],
  initialCapital: 100000,
  currency: "USD",
  commissionType: "cash_per_unit", // percent | cash_per_order | cash_per_unit
  commission: 1.25,
  slippage: 0.25,
  pyramiding: 1,
  maxPositions: 3,
  defaultQtyType: "fixed",          // fixed | percent_equity
  defaultQtyValue: 1,
  from: "2024-01-01",
  to: "2026-12-31"
});
```

`instruments` enables the shared-capital portfolio runtime. The primary `dataset` remains the Strategy decision clock. Each instrument may use dataset metadata or an object specification with `capitalModel`, `marginRate`, `pointValue`, `tickSize`, `quantityStep`, `minQuantity`, `sector`, and v1.8.6 `corporateActions`. `pointValue` / `tickSize` normally come from the relevant dataset unless overridden.

Orders route by dataset:

```kx
strategy.entry("NQ Long", strategy.long, { dataset: "nq_1m" });
strategy.exit("NQ Risk", "NQ Long", { dataset: "nq_1m", stop: stopPrice });
strategy.close("NQ Long", { dataset: "nq_1m" });
```

### Execution timing

The default `executionMode: "ohlc"` uses explicit deterministic semantics:

- logic is evaluated on completed bar N;
- market actions from N execute at N+1 open;
- pending limit/stop entries submitted on N are eligible from N+1 and remain live until filled/cancelled;
- protective instructions from N are active on N+1;
- stop gaps fill from the adverse bar open plus configured slippage;
- limit entries/exits may receive a better bar-open fill when the market gaps through the price;
- if both stop and target are touched and the OHLC path is unknowable, stop wins (conservative assumption);
- optional `from` / `to` bounds restrict broker execution while earlier loaded bars remain available for indicator warm-up.

Partial exits, stop-limit entries, trailing stops and broker-aware control flow are supported. v1.8 adds optional `executionMode: "bar_magnifier" | "trades" | "ticks"` plus `intrabarDataset`. Strategy logic remains on completed primary bars; fills can be reconstructed from the imported execution dataset. OHLC ambiguity remains conservative at whatever execution-data resolution is available.

## Series model

Time-indexed values are first-class typed Series:

```text
Series<number>
Series<boolean>
Series<string>
```

Arithmetic/comparison/conditional operations are pointwise:

```kx
const fast = ta.ema(close, 12);
const slow = ta.ema(close, 26);
const spread = fast - slow;
const bullish = fast > slow;
const previous = close[1];
```

Series-aware `if` conditions create per-bar execution masks. Strategy calls inside those blocks therefore become timestamped strategy signals instead of requiring explicit user loops.

## Universal Dataset model

OHLCV is one schema, not the definition of data in KX. Imported datasets can be classified as:

```text
ohlcv events fundamentals trades ticks mbo custom
```

Arbitrary columns remain available regardless of classification.

### Primary OHLCV

Study/Strategy and optionally standalone Indicator declarations use:

```kx
dataset: "eur_usd_1d"
```

Bare globals then resolve to that dataset:

```text
open high low close volume time
```

### Secondary/arbitrary data

```kx
const earnings = data.dataset("earnings_results");
const actual = earnings.column("eps_actual");
const estimate = earnings.column("eps_estimate");
const surprise = actual - estimate;
```

Timestamped numeric columns become Series; untimed/tabular values remain collections.

If an imported dataset defines an availability timestamp, `data.dataset()` uses that publication/availability timeline by default. This keeps an observation invisible until it was actually available to the strategy. Use `data.dataset("name", { timeline: "event" })` only when the raw event/effective timeline is intentionally required.

### Causal alignment / no lookahead

```kx
const known = data.align(earnings.eps_actual, {
  mode: "previous"
});
```

- `exact` — exact timestamp only
- `previous` — latest observation at/before target (default causal behavior)
- `next` — future observation; requires explicit lookahead permission
- `nearest` — may use future observation; requires explicit lookahead permission

`data.join()` follows the same principle.

### Data operations

```kx
data.dataset(...)
data.available(...)
data.align(...)
data.filter(...)
data.resample(...)
data.join(...)
data.current()
data.security(...)
data.market(...)
```

`data.market(dataset)` is the portfolio-oriented OHLCV accessor. It loads a named market dataset and causally aligns its fields to the current Strategy clock; the same dataset reference can be used in `strategy.entry(..., { dataset })`.

See `DATA_ENGINE.md` for the detailed storage/import contract.

## Standard-library namespaces

Current language surface includes:

- `ta.*`
- `stats.*`
- `math.*`
- `series.*`
- `data.*`
- `input.*`
- `plot.*`
- `pane.*`
- `draw.*`
- `map.*` / collection helpers
- `strategy.*`
- `console.*`
- `emit()`

The v1.8 executable time/session surface includes `time.year`, `time.month`, `time.day`, `time.dayOfMonth`, `time.dayOfWeek`, `time.hour`, `time.minute`, `time.second`, `time.parts()`, `time.timestamp()`, `time.isBetween()`, `time.isAfter()`, `time.isBefore()`, `session.define()`, `session.isOpen()`, `session.isFirstBar()`, and `session.isLastBar()`. Wider catalogue entries should still not be treated as runtime support unless wired into execution/tests.

## Renderer contract

KX never directly calls Lightweight Charts. It emits renderer-neutral plots, panes and drawing descriptors. Chart-native Lightweight Charts primitives keep script drawings attached to price/time scales during zoom, pan and price-scale changes.

Strategy executions are emitted as chart drawing descriptors so entry/exit markers use the same chart object path as other KX drawings.

## Incremental execution

The runtime can retain incremental Series/TA state for attached scripts. Historical prepends deliberately reseed recursive calculations where older data changes later state.

For the current standalone historical Strategy runtime, a Strategy run is deterministic over the declared imported dataset and optional backtest date bounds.

## Safety

KX enforces compute/work, statement, loop, recursion, dataset-request, plot and drawing limits. Debugger waiting/Visual Execution delay is excluded from the compute budget.

Arbitrary OS/network access remains outside the language sandbox.

## Point-in-time datasets and corporate actions — v1.8.6

When an imported dataset defines an availability timestamp, `data.dataset("...")` uses that timeline by default. Use `data.dataset("...", { timeline: "event" })` only when raw occurrence/effective time is intentionally required.

Corporate actions are attached to tradable instrument declarations, not hard-coded to a research method:

```kx
instruments: [{
  dataset: "ASSET_1D",
  corporateActions: ["ASSET_ACTIONS"]
}]
```

The broker supports split/reverse-split, cash-dividend and symbol-change actions. Market dataset adjustment metadata controls obvious double-application protection. Structured order rejection records expose `rejectionCode`, requested capital and available capital where applicable.

## Known Strategy gaps after v1.8.6

Not yet implemented:

- per-instrument bar-magnifier/trades/ticks routing inside portfolio mode (single-instrument v1.8 intrabar execution remains supported)
- cross-currency conversion and advanced margin/maintenance-liquidation rules
- borrow, funding and interest costs
- full exchange trading-calendar/delisting policies beyond v1.8.6 validation/gap flags
- broader release-level regression suite beyond the v1.8.6 integrity fixtures
- parameter sweeps, saved run comparison, walk-forward/out-of-sample research workflow
- Study report API/page and richer decision inspection

Unsupported future APIs should continue to produce diagnostics rather than silently assuming behavior.


## v1.9 research/report additions

Research output is a first-class KX surface:

```kx
report.metric("Metric", value);
report.table("Table", ["A", "B"], rows);
report.line("Series", numericSeries);
report.histogram("Distribution", numericSeries);
```

Research helpers added in v1.9:

```kx
stats.zscore(value, values)
stats.rank(value, values, "desc")
stats.percentileRank(value, values)
```

Strategy declarations may include passive `benchmarks: [...]`. KX `input.*` declarations can attach `group` and `tooltip` metadata consumed by the Inputs panel. Plot `priceScale` values `left`, `right`, and `none` are honored by Chart Preview; `none` uses an independent overlay scale.


## KX 2.0 language freeze

KX 2.0 uses `src/engine/apiRegistry.ts` as the canonical public API contract. The registry is exported to `public/kx-api.json` and is consumed by the editor and documentation site.

### Libraries

```kx
library({ name: "Research Utils" });
function pct(current, previous) { return ((current / previous) - 1) * 100; }
export pct;
```

```kx
import library Utils from "Libraries/Research Utils";
const util = Utils();
```

### Dynamic universes

`data.list({...})` returns Data Library dataset ids/names/symbols/summaries matching generic metadata filters. It is designed for cross-sectional and multi-asset research without hard-coded universe lists.

### Position lifecycle

Strategies may inspect `strategy.positionEntryTime`, `strategy.positionBarsHeld` and their `...Of(dataset)` portfolio variants. These are generic broker-state primitives for time stops, fixed-horizon research, rebalance periods and event-drift holding windows.

### Imported event columns

Dataset transforms address explicit imported columns before same-named dataset metadata. A table may therefore contain a timestamped column named `symbol` and still be filtered with `data.filter(events, { column: "symbol", equals: ... })` while `dataset.symbol` remains the dataset/instrument metadata value.


### Date-only / uncertain publication timing

Generic event/fundamental datasets without an `availabilityColumn` emit `KX6608` when `data.dataset()` would otherwise use raw event time by default. When only a conservative delay is known, shift observability explicitly:

```kx
const events = data.dataset("date_only_events", { delay: "1d" });
```

The delay changes the dataset observation timeline; it does not rewrite the original source row. This is useful for conservative date-only releases and other lagged information while preserving the raw/effective event timestamp for separate analysis.

guides.title: Host integration
guides.description: Embed Studio and connect workspace, data and chart services.
guides.markdown:
# Standalone architecture and host integration

KX Studio is now developed as a standalone application.

The previous host-injection architecture is retained internally because modular boundaries are useful, but the product no longer assumes that a separate main Kinetix application will provide its chart/data/workspace services.

## Standalone service boundaries

```text
KX Studio
  ├─ Monaco / IDE shell
  ├─ KX compiler + interpreter
  ├─ local Dataset Library
  │    ├─ CSV/TSV importer
  │    ├─ schema/role inference
  │    └─ IndexedDB persistence
  ├─ StandaloneDataBridge
  │    ├─ active OHLCV dataset
  │    ├─ arbitrary named datasets
  │    └─ market-data lifecycle events
  ├─ Lightweight Charts preview/chart surface
  └─ local workspace persistence
```

The interfaces in `src/services/contracts.ts` keep host boundaries separate from KX semantics. The desktop app now implements Tauri workspace persistence, native DuckDB plans, secure provider connections and acquisition jobs alongside the compatible browser/IndexedDB bridge. Visual preparation and generated KX share those same services; this is not a separate transformation runtime.

## Data abstraction

`MarketDataset` remains backward compatible for the active OHLCV chart.

`GenericDataset` represents arbitrary tabular/timestamped data.

`KinetixDataset = MarketDataset | GenericDataset` is the runtime-level union used by KX dataset objects.

See `DATA_ENGINE.md` for language semantics.
